topics.title: Claude Security: A Multi-Agent Vulnerability Scanner That Lives in Your Terminal
topics.whyTrending: Anthropic's Claude Security plugin came out of closed preview into open beta for all Claude Code users. It runs a coordinated agent set that maps the codebase, reasons about threats, correlates issues across files and business logic, independently double-checks findings, then emits patch files you review and apply. Scans recent changes or a whole repo using inference you're already paying for. Nobody has written the honest 'what it actually catches vs what it misses vs Semgrep/CodeQL' piece, and it's the natural sequel to the keyv hardening post.

topics.title: Kimi K3 Tops the Frontend Arena — and Ranks 4th on Intelligence. Both Are True.
topics.whyTrending: Moonshot's K3 (July 2026) is the first open 3T-class model: 2.8T params, 16 of 896 experts active per token, 1M context, Kimi Delta Attention for 6.3x faster decoding. It's #1 on Arena.ai's Frontend Code Arena — the first open model to lead frontend coding, ahead of Fable 5 — and scores 93.4% SWE-bench Verified on Vals AI's harness. But it's #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (57.11 vs Fable 5's 59.86), and researchers are flagging hallucination behaviour the benchmarks don't capture. A benchmark-literacy piece with real numbers, following the Terminal-Bench post's lineage.

topics.title: Claude Code Design Mode: The Figma-Screenshot-to-React Loop, Honestly Assessed
topics.whyTrending: The frontend-design plugin plus the in-app browser closes the design→code→verify loop inside the terminal: /frontend-design renders live HTML/CSS/JS from prose, accepts Figma screenshots as pixel references, and the browser lets Claude navigate, screenshot and annotate specific elements by appearance rather than DOM structure. The community workflow is stabilising around Design → Craft → A11y → Perf with /baseline-ui and /fixing-accessibility. Directly on-brand for a frontend blog and almost entirely covered by hype posts rather than real evaluations.

topics.title: Cursor 3's Agents Window vs Claude Code: Two Bets on What an Agent Console Is
topics.whyTrending: Cursor 3 (April 2, 2026) repositioned the product as an agent orchestration console that also edits code — Agents Window running parallel agents across local machines, worktrees, cloud sandboxes and remote SSH from one pane, plus Cloud Agents in isolated VMs with pre-warmed builds that start 3x faster. Claude Code answered from the other direction with self-hosted runners and nested subagents. This is an architecture comparison, not a feature bake-off: where should agent execution live, and who owns the environment?

topics.title: Subagent Forking Is Now the Default: What Changed in Claude Code's Multi-Agent Model
topics.whyTrending: August 2026 releases made subagent forking the default, upgraded SendMessage, and added cross-session mentions so agents in different sessions can address each other. Combined with per-subagent model control from the Opus 5 move, the primitives for multi-agent work have shifted materially since anything written earlier this year. Also: the agent view now distinguishes 'Needs input' from 'Working' — a small change with real implications for anyone measuring agent throughput.

topics.title: Baseline 2026: The CSS You Can Finally Ship Without a Fallback
topics.whyTrending: Container style queries, contrast-color(), the shape() function for clip-path and offset-path, the :open pseudo-class and custom highlights all reached Baseline Newly Available in 2026. shape() in particular replaces unreadable polygon() coordinate soup with move/line/curve commands that accept CSS units and math functions. Concrete, code-heavy, evergreen, and a genuine 'delete your fallback' moment rather than another 'CSS features you should know' listicle.

topics.title: Inference Got Cheap. Your Agent Architecture Is Still Optimized for 2025.
topics.whyTrending: Opus 5 landed in July at roughly half the flagship price with a per-request effort dial, OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 pricing by up to 80%, and open weights are now cheap enough to run coding agents for cents. Every architectural decision built around token scarcity — aggressive context trimming, single-pass generation, skipping verification because it doubles cost — was priced for a market that no longer exists. The contrarian follow-through: spend the savings on redundant verification, not longer contexts.

topics.title: A Custom Video Player With Zero JavaScript State, Thanks to Chrome 152
topics.whyTrending: Chrome 152 shipped :playing, :paused, :seeking, :buffering, :stalled, :muted and :volume-locked — media state as CSS pseudo-classes, and an Interop 2026 focus area so the other engines are following. Every custom player today syncs state into class names with JavaScript event listeners; this deletes that layer. Also in 152: relative alpha colors and the window-drag property for installed PWAs. A build-along post with a working player and no state sync at all.

topics.title: Server-Supplied Hooks and Gateway Policy: Governing a Self-Hosted Agent Fleet
topics.whyTrending: v2.1.229 (Aug 12) added server-supplied Claude Code hook support for self-hosted runner sessions so they match managed-environment behaviour, and gateway spend-limit messages now name the cap, its reset time and the operator's message. Together with policy and marketplace validation improvements, this is the missing governance layer for the self-hosted fleets that shipped ten days earlier — how you enforce policy on runners you operate but don't want developers editing.

topics.title: SWE-bench Is Solved. SWE-EVO Says Your Agent Still Can't Maintain Software.
topics.whyTrending: With frontier and open models both clearing 93% on SWE-bench Verified, the benchmark has stopped discriminating. SWE-EVO benchmarks coding agents on long-horizon software evolution — multi-commit feature work against a moving codebase — which is what people actually do all day and where scores collapse. A follow-up to the Terminal-Bench piece, arguing that single-issue-fix benchmarks are now measuring a solved problem while the real gap stays unmeasured.
